title: Completed local rings represent marked Artinian scheme points
statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] and let $Y\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ be a scheme locally of finite type [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $y\in Y$ have residue field $k=\kappa(y)$ finite as an $R$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module, def-weil-field, def-weil-residue-field]. Put $C=\widehat{\mathcal O_{Y,y}}=\varprojlim_{n\geq1}\mathcal O_{Y,y}/\mathfrak m_y^n$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. A local ring means a ring with a unique maximal ideal, a local homomorphism means one whose inverse image of the target maximal ideal is the source maximal ideal, and an Artinian ring satisfies the descending chain condition on ideals. Then $C$ is a complete Noetherian local $R$-algebra with residue field canonically $k$, and $C/\mathfrak m_C^n$ is Artinian local with residue field $k$ for each $n\geq1$. For every Artinian local $R$-algebra $A$ with specified residue field $k$, composition with the canonical map $\operatorname{Spec}C\to Y$ gives a bijection
$$\{v:C\to A\mid v\text{ is a local }R\text{-map inducing }1_k\}\ \xrightarrow{\sim}\ \{a:\operatorname{Spec}A\to Y\text{ over }R\mid a|_{\operatorname{Spec}k}=y\},$$
where on the right $y$ denotes the canonical residue-field morphism. Every $v$ on the left kills some $\mathfrak m_C^n$, and the bijection is natural in local $R$-maps between the test algebras inducing $1_k$. Under it, maps $C\to C/\mathfrak m_C^n$ correspond to the canonical infinitesimal neighbourhood maps to $Y$, compatibly with their quotient transition maps.

source.place: Tag 0CXK (lemma-versality-matches), proof: completion belongs to the category of complete Noetherian local test algebras and the displayed identification of maps from the completion with scheme-valued Artinian points.

proof.text: Put $B=\mathcal O_{Y,y}$ and $\mathfrak m=\mathfrak m_y$. By the definition of locally finite type, choose an affine neighbourhood $U=\operatorname{Spec}T$ of $y$ with $T$ a finite type $R$-algebra. The finite-type Noetherian theorem makes $T$ Noetherian. The affine-stalk localization theorem identifies $B$ with $T_{\mathfrak p_y}$, so the localization Noetherian theorem makes $B$ Noetherian. It is local with residue field $k$ by the definition of the scheme residue field. In particular $\mathfrak m$ is finitely generated, by the definition of Noetherian ring. This uses only locally finite type; no quasi-compactness of $Y$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 0CXK (lemma-versality-matches), first sentence of proof; Algebra Tag 00FN (lemma-Noetherian-permanence) and Schemes Tag 01J6 (lemma-morphism-from-spec-local-ring), affine-stalk description

proof.text: Let $\iota:B\to C$ be the completion map and $p_n:C\to B/\mathfrak m^n$ its coordinate projection. The local-completion theorem gives that $C$ is local, with maximal ideal $\mathfrak n=\mathfrak m C=\ker p_1$ and canonical residue field $k$. The Noetherian-completion theorem gives that $C$ is Noetherian. Apply the module-completion theorem with base ring $B$, ideal $\mathfrak m$, and module $M=B$: its completion is the underlying $B$-module of $C$, and it is complete for the submodules $\mathfrak m^n C$. Since $\mathfrak n^n=(\mathfrak m C)^n=\mathfrak m^n C$ (both are finite sums of products $\iota(b_1)\cdots\iota(b_n)c$), this is precisely completeness for powers of the maximal ideal of $C$. The structure map $R\to B\to C$ makes it a complete Noetherian local $R$-algebra.

For every $n\geq1$, the same module-completion theorem says that $p_n$ is surjective and $\ker p_n=\mathfrak m^n C=\mathfrak n^n$. It is a ring homomorphism by the componentwise ring operations of the completion. Thus $p_n$ identifies $C/\mathfrak n^n$ with $B/\mathfrak m^n$ as rings and as $R$-algebras: $p_n\iota(b)=b\bmod\mathfrak m^n$. These identifications commute with quotient maps because the coordinate at $n$ is the reduction of every higher coordinate. Apply the Noetherian-local quotient theorem to $C$, $K=\mathfrak n^n$ and $N=n$. Its hypotheses hold since $\mathfrak n^n\subseteq\mathfrak n$ for $n\geq1$. Hence $C/\mathfrak n^n$ is Artinian local. Its maximal ideal is $\mathfrak n/\mathfrak n^n$, whose quotient is $C/\mathfrak n=k$, so it has the asserted residue field.

source.place: Tag 05GG (lemma-hathat-finitely-generated), all positive exponents; Tag 00KH (lemma-Noetherian-dimension-0), applied as in Tag 02HT (lemma-smooth-test-artinian)

proof.text: Fix a marked Artinian local $R$-algebra $A$, and write $q_A:A\to k$ for its specified residue map and $q_B:B\to k$ for the canonical one. The local-spectrum correspondence identifies maps $a:\operatorname{Spec}A\to Y$ whose closed point maps to $y$ with local maps $u:B\to A$. Fix an affine neighbourhood $U=\operatorname{Spec}T$ of $y$. Every prime of a local ring lies in its maximal ideal, so if $f\notin\mathfrak m_A$ then $f$ lies in no prime of $A$; hence an open subset of $\operatorname{Spec}A$ containing the closed point is all of $\operatorname{Spec}A$. Applied to $a^{-1}(U)$, this shows that every such $a$ factors through $U$, and the same argument for the local ring $B$ shows that every morphism $\operatorname{Spec}B\to Y$ sending the closed point to $y$ factors through $U$. On $U$, this correspondence is the map $T\to B\xrightarrow{u}A$, by the affine-stalk localization description and the uniqueness of the local-spectrum correspondence. The contravariant bijection for affine spectra therefore says that $a$ is over $R$ exactly when $u$ commutes with the structure maps from $R$. Restricting to $\operatorname{Spec}k$ replaces that ring map by its composite with $q_A$. Consequently the marking condition is exactly $q_Au=q_B$; equality on $T$ implies equality on $B=T_{\mathfrak p_y}$ because fractions are determined by their numerators and the inverses of their denominators. Thus the right-hand set in the item is identified with local $R$-maps $u:B\to A$ inducing $1_k$. In particular, applying the correspondence to the identity $B\to B$ gives the canonical $c:\operatorname{Spec}B\to Y$, and the canonical map used in the statement is $c\circ\operatorname{Spec}\iota$.

source.place: Tag 01J6 (lemma-morphism-from-spec-local-ring), construction and affine case; Equation 02NA (equation-canonical-morphism); used in artin.tex Tag 0CXK

proof.text: By the Artinian-local nilpotence theorem choose $N\geq1$ with $\mathfrak m_A^N=0$. If $u:B\to A$ is local, then $u(\mathfrak m)\subseteq\mathfrak m_A$, so $u(\mathfrak m^N)=0$. Define $\bar u:B/\mathfrak m^N\to A$ by $\bar u(b\bmod\mathfrak m^N)=u(b)$, and set $\widetilde u=\bar u\,p_N:C\to A$. This is an $R$-map with $\widetilde u\,\iota=u$. Its composite with $q_A$ is $p_1:C\to k$, since $q_Au=q_B$ and the coordinates reduce compatibly; hence $\widetilde u^{-1}(\mathfrak m_A)=\ker p_1=\mathfrak n$, making it local and residue-preserving. Conversely every local $v:C\to A$ kills $\mathfrak n^N$, since it takes each factor from $\mathfrak n$ into $\mathfrak m_A$. For $x\in C$ choose $b\in B$ representing $p_N(x)\in B/\mathfrak m^N$. Then $x-\iota(b)\in\ker p_N=\mathfrak n^N$, so $v(x)=v\iota(b)$. Therefore restriction along $\iota$ is injective on these local maps, and the displayed construction is its inverse. This also proves independence of the exponent $N$, without imposing a separate continuity hypothesis on $v$.

source.place: Tag 0CXK (lemma-versality-matches), displayed identification of Artinian points, with its completion extension argument expanded using Algebra Tags 00J8 and 05GG

proof.text: Combine steps 4 and 5. A residue-preserving local $v:C\to A$ restricts to the local map $v\iota:B\to A$ (the residue kernels are $\mathfrak m$ and $\mathfrak m_A$). Its corresponding scheme map is $c\circ\operatorname{Spec}(v\iota)=(c\circ\operatorname{Spec}\iota)\circ\operatorname{Spec}v$, by functoriality of the affine spectrum and the local-spectrum bijection. This is exactly the map in the statement, so it is bijective. If $h:A\to A'$ is a local $R$-map inducing $1_k$, then $(hv)\iota=h(v\iota)$. Both the ring-map construction and the scheme-map construction therefore send $v$ to $hv$ and $a$ to $a\circ\operatorname{Spec}h$, respectively. This gives the required naturality for every such $h$, whether or not $h$ is surjective.

source.place: Tag 0CXK (lemma-versality-matches), identification of predeformation categories and its displayed equality of sets

proof.text: Take $A=C/\mathfrak n^n$ with its residue marking and let $v_n:C\to A$ be the quotient map. By step 3 its composite with $\iota$ is the canonical quotient $B\to B/\mathfrak m^n$, followed by the inverse of the coordinate isomorphism $C/\mathfrak n^n\cong B/\mathfrak m^n$. Step 4 therefore sends $v_n$ to the canonical infinitesimal neighbourhood map $\operatorname{Spec}(B/\mathfrak m^n)\to\operatorname{Spec}B\xrightarrow{c}Y$ under this identification. For $r\geq n\geq1$ the quotient transition $h_{r,n}:C/\mathfrak n^r\to C/\mathfrak n^n$ satisfies $h_{r,n}v_r=v_n$. By step 6 its corresponding morphisms satisfy $a_n=a_r\circ\operatorname{Spec}h_{r,n}$. The identity also holds for $r=n$, proving all the stipulated compatibility clauses.
